title: Porneia: "Sexual Sin" and "Prostitution"
lead: The Greek word family pornē (prostitute), porneia (sexual sin) and porneuō covered prostitution and, by the first century, any sex outside marriage. In the Greek Old Testament it translates Hebrew zanah, which the prophets use for Israel's idolatry and for trade with the nations (Hosea 1–3; Ezekiel 16; Isaiah 23:15–18; Numbers 25:1). In the New Testament it is the "exception" in Jesus's teaching on divorce (Matthew 5:32; Matthew 19:9), one of the things the apostles' decree forbids (Acts 15:20, 29), and Revelation's word for Babylon (Revelation 17–18).
